messages:
nina: FYI ran into an annoying MSI installer behavior on Win10 today. Installer created a new default profile and skipped migrating my old `profiles.yaml` under `%APPDATA%\\Redwood` so all my saved endpoints disappeared. anyone seen this?

paul: ugh. which installer did you use? our MSI should migrate user config from old locations.

nina: downloaded the stable MSI from the releases page (v1.8.2). After install `redwoodctl profile list` showed only `default` and not my old `work`/`personal` profiles. Installer logs show a migration step but it exited with code 0 and no files were copied.

kevin: any permissions errors? sometimes the installer runs as SYSTEM and can't access the user's roaming profile if they were logged out during install.

nina: installer log snippet: ```
[2024-09-05 10:02:31] migrate: scanning C:\\Users\\nina\\AppData\\Roaming\\Redwood\\profiles.yaml
[2024-09-05 10:02:31] migrate: found legacy config, attempting move
[2024-09-05 10:02:31] migrate: copy failed: access denied
```

paul: yep that's the issue. Our MSI upgrade path runs as elevated and tries to read the user profile but sometimes Windows blocks cross-user access. We should detect that and fall back to creating a per-user migration helper that runs on first launch as the installing user.

kevin: short-term workaround for nina: run `redwoodctl config import --from "%APPDATA%\\Redwood\\profiles.yaml"` as your user to recover profiles. We'll add a `redwoodctl config migrate --from-legacy` command to help automate.

nina: thanks, that worked. Two follow-ups: 1) the UI for profile switching is confusing in CLI output when you have many named profiles (the `*` marker is easy to miss). 2) after I reimported profiles, `redwoodctl login` failed with device-code behind corp proxy until I unset `HTTPS_PROXY`. It seems related to previous threads about device-code + proxy.

paul: good catch. For (1) we can improve `redwoodctl profile list` to show current profile in bold or add a `--current` flag. For (2) we should print a clearer hint when device-code polling gets repeated 401s: detect `HTTPS_PROXY` and suggest `try unsetting HTTPS_PROXY or use --auth-method browser`.

ops-bot: Note: Installer team notified by @paul. Package owners: please review the migration fallback proposal.

kevin: also consider adding a telemetry ping on first-run migration failures (opt-in) so we can see how frequently this happens across installs. no sensitive data, just a code signal.

nina: one more oddity: when I run `redwoodctl --config-path "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Temp\\rwcfg" whoami` it worked fine, but `redwoodctl --profile work api whoami` picked the wrong endpoint from an earlier default profile that had the same name but different casing (Work vs work). Our profile lookup should be case-insensitive for names.

paul: agreed. treat profile names as case-insensitive keys but preserve original casing for display. Add an integration test around profile name collisions.

ci-bot: Issue created: INF-3102 "windows msi: fallback user-migration helper; config import command; profile lookup case-insensitivity; device-code proxy hint" assigned to @paul.

kevin: i'll open a PR with three small CLI fixes: 1) `config import` subcommand, 2) `profile list --current` UX, 3) case-insensitive lookup. Will include unit tests.

nina: thanks! will validate the import tool and profile UX once PR is merged. tagging `msi`, `profiles`, `config-migrate`, `device-code`, `proxy` for search.
